posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
So this week's challenge is Mad Bomber Blade vs Young Legacy, G.I. Bunker, SS Tachyon and Rook City Wraith in Megalopolis, a relatively easy challenge to start us off.

Mint!

No damage from Bunker

Foam Grenade, Foam Grenade, Heavy Plating, Flak Cannon (no power due to Paparazzi) game won on Wraith's turn. But stopping the environment was really useful. It gave Tachyon a chance to get 12 Burst cards in the trash for double Lightspeed Barrage on her last turn.

The Wraith proved her usual self, setting up with Razor Ordnance and Micro Targeting Computer on the first and second turn, then losing both to Blade's flip and setting back up with Throwing Knives & MTC on her third turn and Razor Ordnance on her fourth, leading to her getting the kill.

Huzzah for (my) heroes, how did yours do?

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Similar success, though I think my Bunker used Flak Cannon once.  I didn't use foam grenade, but Wraith's base power on the first turn allowed me to avoid a dreaded hostage situation. Otherwise, Bunker's base power proved very useful to bust through Blade's double force fields.

 

Tachyon liberally used Hypersonic assault, once staving off what would have been a particularly nasty Devious Disruption.

 

Wraith and Legacy dealt most of the damage through MTC-boosted razor ordinance and Legacy's one-shots and base power, though Tachyon delivered the victory blow with a 13-point Lightspeed Barrage.

 

fun! Thanks!

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
I ended up with Infrared Eyepiece in the opening draw, which basically meant the game was a cakewalk -- he only had two cards under him when he flipped, and only managed to get two in the trash on his other side. Tachyon ended up just discarding a chunk of Legacy's deck before finally finding Inspiring Presence, and the one time I Experimented on her ended up giving me Environment destruction when needed. Bunker just got stuck with cruddy cards for most of it, so he stuck to keeping the environment in check. Young Legacy finished him off very thematically -- putting on her dad's ring then a double shot of Motivational Charge and Atomic Glare.

Wraith had real lucky draws -- in addition to starting with the Eyepiece, using it got her Impromptu Invention. Using it her next turn got her...another Impromptu invention. With the Stun Bolt and Targetting Computer already in hand, all I needed to actually get from the deck was the Utility Belt and she was all set to go two rounds in.

posts.name: ClericalError
posts.cooked:
I can see why you would want Fixed Decks. This particular One Shot (if using Randomised Decks) could prove incredibly luck-based issues. 6 Targets go under Bomber Blade in the first turn for one player and none for another player? You're gonna see some resentment from the completionists and collectors out there.

It does have the little problem that people can log on, see the deck order and use someone else's strategy to get Mint without posing a challenge, but seeing as you highlighted in your article that this was to "build the community" then I don't see that as TOO big an issue. If too many people are using online posts to get Mint Comics that means that your plan worked well. The community is working together to figure this stuff out.

Personally, this wasn't really a challenge with the cards that came up, but the Theme was fantastic. I'd prefer that these One Shots remain less difficult than these games have the potential to be as it will help players who are new to the game be able to collect the Mint Issues without HAVING to look up a guide and will be less likely to make the Community not risk losing their Mint because they didn't look it up! If they chose to play a certain character aggressively instead of defensively that one hypothetical turn where it mattered a lot.

 

PS. I love how this One Shot was really a showcase of how Bunker is covering Megalopolis paparazzi with Adhesive Foam! lol. Move along citizens, nothing to see here.
